nodes.body: The post loft behind the gatehouse smells of old seed and iron. It's a dusty, sweet smell that gets in your hair. There are 68 brass message capsules in wire racks, piled high. A loop of spare cord hangs from a hook. On the bench, a logbook has THE CIRCUIT written on top in marker. Outside, the wall-top path climbs between the battlements into low mist. The south-gate bell says it is a quarter past three.

choices.label: Take the ledger and pick a section of the wall.

nodes.body: Master Fenn sits on an old seed crate with a bandage on his hand. He reads the circuit out loud, but half of it is already wrong. The Alders moved their loft two winters ago, so the roll of cord is not where the page says. The wall above the old break is not the path in the note. The Guild bell rings to shut the city gates at sunset. The circuit has three parts, and there is only one afternoon to do them all.

choices.label: Start at the Tower Stairs.
Start at the Ropewalk Bends.
Start at the Market Stile.

nodes.body: The Tower Stairs are 114 stone steps cut into the inner wall. There is a capsule bracket every sixth step. A storm last spring ripped four brackets clean out of the stone, and the tenth step from the bottom has crumbled away. Every tray has to come up by hand. Nothing rolls on these stairs.

choices.label: Look at the loose brackets first.
Deal with the broken step.
Cycle the trays up before the light shifts.

nodes.body: The Ropewalk Bends are where the wall-top path was moved because the old wall fell down in the winter rains. The circuit still lists a stretch of wall the pigeons do not use, and says nothing about the one they do use. The Weaver keeps his dye vats in the yard crossed by the new path. He has locked the gate with three loops of chain.

choices.label: Look at the chained gate.
Ride to the old breach and see what is left.
Go and find the Weaver.

nodes.body: The Market Stile is the bottom of the route where fourteen capsules hang in old lime trees. The branches are heavy with un-picked nuts. The stile digs a groove in the cobbles. Last spring, someone hung the capsules so low that a porter put a sack right through one.

choices.label: See to the dragging stile.
Sort out the low branches.
Deal with the fallen nuts.

nodes.body: Four brackets lie in the dust between the steps with their rivets still in them. The holes in the stone are now bigger than the rivets that fell out. A fifth bracket turns in its hole like a loose tooth. The storm that did this is promised again tonight as a grey wall of cloud rolls in from the sea.

choices.label: Hunt down the pot of rock putty.
Wire the brackets in instead.
Ask Mira what the chandlery has.

nodes.body: The tenth step from the bottom is gone. The gap drops to your knee onto loose cement. In the afternoon light, anyone can see it. After dark, it sits exactly where a tired rider puts a foot down. Behind the loft, there is one flat board, four bricks, and half a sack of wet plaster dust.

choices.label: Hunt down the pot of rock putty.
Wire the brackets in instead.
Ask Mira what the chandlery has.

nodes.body: Sixty-eight capsules weigh nothing on their own, but together they are very heavy. The wire trays need both hands each. The sky chalk board at the harbour says squalls will arrive after five. Lottie can pull her cart as far as the first landing, but the last three hundred stairs must be carried by hand.

choices.label: Hunt down the pot of rock putty.
Wire the brackets in instead.
Ask Mira what the chandlery has.

nodes.body: The gate to the new path is shut with three loops of chain. A note in chalk says the gate must stay locked. The dye vats steam in the far corner under a thin blue mist. The stile by the gate is missing one board, and another board is green with damp.

choices.label: Work out where the capsules go now.
Find something to hang the new ones on.
Make the turn obvious in the dim.

nodes.body: The old path stops at a lip of bare stone where the wall gave way last February. Below it, the wall drops straight down. No one should walk so close to that edge in the dark. The circuit still lists eleven capsules hung along the part that is gone.

choices.label: Work out where the capsules go now.
Find something to hang the new ones on.
Make the turn obvious in the dim.

nodes.body: The Weaver is somewhere between the dye shed and the drying loft. He has said twice this year that the Guild uses his yard like a road. He is also the only person with a cart and a spare spool of twine. He has never once lost a message on his stretch of the wall.

choices.label: Work out where the capsules go now.
Find something to hang the new ones on.
Make the turn obvious in the dim.

nodes.body: The market stile makes a groove in the cobbles and takes both hands and a shoulder to move. This is fine at three o'clock, but it is hard when you carry a bag at sunset. The hinge pin is worn to a silver shine, and the post itself leans into the wall.

choices.label: Rehang the hooks where they belong.
Light the last stretch into the market.
Take the twins up on their offer.

nodes.body: Last spring, someone hung the market pods under branches thick with nuts. The pods were at head height. A porter pushed his sack right through one and got a face full of dust. The trees have grown since then, but the nuts are still there. The same hooks now hang even lower.

choices.label: Rehang the hooks where they belong.
Light the last stretch into the market.
Take the twins up on their offer.

nodes.body: Fallen nuts lie deep under the two old trees near the gate. The wasps in the nuts are slow and cross in the cool air. No one wants to reach up into a tree above all that. There is a handcart behind the wall, and clearing the mess takes about twenty minutes of good light.

choices.label: Rehang the hooks where they belong.
Light the last stretch into the market.
Take the twins up on their offer.

nodes.body: The pot of rock putty is not on its shelf. Master Fenn saw it go up the stairs last fall, but it never came back down. This means it is either lost in the ivy at the top landing or left in the back of a stable in the lower ward.

choices.label: Set the whole flight before the light goes.
Hang one capsule and watch it in the wind.
Go down and tell Master Fenn what the stairs need.

nodes.body: There is a tray with two arm lengths of cord. Master Fenn shows a way to hold a bracket with his good hand. Twist, then tuck the sharp end down. Never leave a loop where a sleeve can catch. It holds for a season. Everyone who has done it says so with a look.

choices.label: Measure the stairs and write them up properly.
Set the whole flight before the light goes.
Hang one capsule and watch it in the wind.

nodes.body: The candle shop keeps a drawer of odd bits under the counter. Mira will find a use for anything in it, if you tell her the job. She also has firm views on the wall-top, a spare kettle, and the only cord-waxer in the city that does not jam.

choices.label: Go down and tell Master Fenn what the stairs need.
Measure the stairs and write them up properly.
Set the whole flight before the light goes.

nodes.body: The new walk is forty paces higher than the old one. It turns twice, where the old one ran straight. Eleven pods in the old spots would mark a path that ends at a drop. The new path needs nine pods. Two of those spots have nothing to hang them on.

choices.label: Cycle the new line carrying a tray.
Get the gate question settled properly.
Mark the drop above the old breach.

nodes.body: There are no trees on the turn. There is no wall for a hundred paces. The fence posts belong to the Weaver. The loft can give us three bamboo poles. It also has a bundle of stakes for bean plants, and a mallet with a split handle.

choices.label: Leave the turn for the Guild-masters and go back down.
Cycle the new line carrying a tray.
Get the gate question settled properly.

nodes.body: A runner coming down in dim light will follow the wall that seems most walked. That is still the old edge. No matter what else happens on this wall, we must mark the turn. It has to be clear at dusk to a tired person who has stopped reading the stone.

choices.label: Mark the drop above the old breach.
Leave the turn for the Guild-masters and go back down.
Cycle the new line carrying a tray.

nodes.body: A market pod must be high enough. It must clear the tallest porter carrying a sack. It must be below any branch that can whip in a gust. To find that spot, you must stand where the porters walk and look up. Do not just stand where the ladder is.

choices.label: Hang the market stretch before dusk.
Cycle the market the way a messenger would.
Take the spare capsules up the wall.

nodes.body: The last forty paces before the gate are the part everyone forgets. From there, you can already see the market lights. That spot also has the worst ground. There is a deep rut, a drain grate, and a corner where lime trees hide the turn.

choices.label: Finish the market beautifully and stop there.
Hang the market stretch before dusk.
Cycle the market the way a messenger would.

nodes.body: Kit and Ren are nine years old. They have stood at the gate for ten minutes, hoping for a job. They can easily carry, count, and tell the truth about how many pods are left. They cannot be quiet, and we cannot trust them with the mallet.

choices.label: Take the spare capsules up the wall.
Finish the market beautifully and stop there.
Hang the market stretch before dusk.

nodes.body: The stairs take one capsule every sixth bracket, twenty in all, and hanging from the bottom up means cycling past everything already hung, while hanging from the top down means walking back down through the dim with nothing marked behind.

choices.label: Get the twine sorted first.
Get more hands onto the wall.
Cycle the whole route once, end to end.

nodes.body: One capsule goes up on the fifth bracket and swings there. The way it swings tells you how the other nineteen will act. The wind on the stairs comes across the wall, not up it. The circuit does not say this anywhere on the page.

choices.label: Get ahead of the wind.
Send word up to the Guild messengers.
Mark the bottom of the route now.

nodes.body: In one version of this afternoon, someone cycles back down and says clearly what the stairs need and how long that really takes. In another version, nobody says it until dark. Master Fenn is at the loft with his hand propped up and the kettle on.

choices.label: Get the twine sorted first.
Get more hands onto the wall.
Cycle the whole route once, end to end.

nodes.body: Cycling the new line with a tray is the only way to learn it. It takes twelve minutes at a working pace with the wind pushing from the left. The light on the wall has already gone amber. The cloud is coming down, not lifting.

choices.label: Get ahead of the wind.
Send word up to the Guild messengers.
Mark the bottom of the route now.

nodes.body: There is a difference between cutting the chain and being handed the key. That difference lasts much longer than tonight. The Weaver is at the dye sheds until the vat is drained. The capsule circuit has needed his yard every spring for as long as the ledger has been kept.

choices.label: Get the twine sorted first.
Get more hands onto the wall.
Cycle the whole route once, end to end.

nodes.body: The lip of the old breach is the one place on the whole circuit where being wrong costs more than a twisted ankle. Two capsules and a pole will say stop here to someone who has stopped thinking. There are two capsules spare only if the stairs turn out not to need them.

choices.label: Get ahead of the wind.
Send word up to the Guild messengers.
Mark the bottom of the route now.

nodes.body: Fourteen capsules hang in eleven trees, and one tree takes two. Each one is sealed by hand from a wax stick. This is because the market is the one place on the circuit where the wind cannot reach and the pigeons somehow can.

choices.label: Get the twine sorted first.
Get more hands onto the wall.
Cycle the whole route once, end to end.

nodes.body: Cycling the market from the wall end at a messenger's pace shows the hanging from the way it is used. This is the opposite of the way it was hung. From that side, two capsules turn out to be behind branches and one is behind a trunk.

choices.label: Get ahead of the wind.
Send word up to the Guild messengers.
Mark the bottom of the route now.

nodes.body: The market needs fourteen capsules and the tray holds eighteen. Four spare capsules at the top of the wall are worth much more than four spare capsules in a tray at the bottom of it. Cycling them up now costs the last of the easy light.

choices.label: Get the twine sorted first.
Get more hands onto the wall.
Cycle the whole route once, end to end.

nodes.body: The brackets get measured, and the gap gets drawn to scale. The whole of the Tower Stairs becomes one honest page pinned to the loft door. The capsules go up a week later on proper fixings with someone else cycling. It is not the afternoon anyone planned, and it is not nothing.

ending.title: The Stairs Get Their Own Page

nodes.body: The chain stays on the gate and the new line stays unmarked. So at four, the circuit gets called round the city. Two Guild-masters walk the turn with hand lamps all evening. Nobody comes to harm and nobody thanks anyone. The ledger goes back into its wrap exactly as wrong as it came out.

The market ends up marked properly and prettily, but the wall above it does not. So the messengers come in from the north road by lamplight. They meet the capsules only in the last five minutes of the way home. It looks like a welcome, but it was meant to be a route.

The circuit says the wax sticks live in the loft cupboard. The loft cupboard now holds seed sacks. There are five sticks in a box behind the chandlery. The rest is wherever last spring left it. Sixty-eight capsules seal rather more than five sticks between them.

choices.label: Track down the rest of the wax.
Set up somewhere to seal them.
Go through the seals before filling anything.

nodes.body: Thirteen people in the city have hung capsules before. About seven of them are in on a Tuesday. Asking costs time now. But it buys time later. The names list on the circuit has not been true since the spring before last.

choices.label: Knock on the doors that used to say yes.
Catch people at the school gate.
Put the word out through the chandlery.

nodes.body: No one has cycled the whole loop today. The map shows a path that has changed in two spots since it was written. Forty minutes of cycling would answer more questions than an hour of guessing in the loft.

choices.label: Cycle the route with the ledger and a pencil.
Find the dim gaps between capsules.
Look at what the rain has made of the parapet top.

nodes.body: The wind that came over the wall at three is now bending the lime tree by the gate. Brass capsules and wind have a long, costly past in this city. The loft has a box of storm guards. They fit less than half the capsules.

choices.label: Track down the rest of the wax.
Set up somewhere to seal them.
Go through the seals before filling anything.

nodes.body: Aisling is bringing sixteen messengers in from the north road. She thinks the wall will be marked by sunset. There is one bar of signal at the top of the stairs and none in the market. The message she needs is not the one that says all is well.

choices.label: Knock on the doors that used to say yes.
Catch people at the school gate.
Put the word out through the chandlery.

nodes.body: Marking from the bottom up keeps the done work behind you all afternoon. It shows the messengers the best part last. It also means that when a problem hits at five, the marked part is the one closest to the city, the phone, and the kettle.

choices.label: Cycle the route with the ledger and a pencil.
Find the dim gaps between capsules.
Look at what the rain has made of the parapet top.

nodes.body: Five sticks behind the chandlery. A half box in the gatehouse boiler room that may be sealing wax or lamp wax. And a full box that Master Fenn swears went to the school for the fest hangings and never came back.

choices.label: Go to the school for the missing box.
Ration what there is across the route.
Seal one for twenty minutes and watch it.

nodes.body: Sealing sixty-eight capsules needs a wax stick, a cloth, a flat spot, and a firm rule on where the sealed ones go. Doing it on a tailgate in the wind is how a city ends up with wax grit down the inside of every tray it owns.

choices.label: Ask the city for anything that seals.
Seal fast and get the trays moving.
Go to the school for the missing box.

nodes.body: A seal that has sat in a loft for a year cracks in the first cold and lets the damp in. There are two boxes of new seals in the drawer cut to the wrong length. Trimming sixty-eight of them takes an hour no one has when half of them do not need it.

choices.label: Ration what there is across the route.
Seal one for twenty minutes and watch it.
Ask the city for anything that seals.

nodes.body: The names list is three years old. It reads like a map of who has moved away. Four of the doors are still the right doors. Two of those open onto someone who has been waiting a long time to be asked again.

choices.label: Split whoever comes into teams.
Show the new ones how a bracket holds.
Bring the Weaver in properly.

nodes.body: The school gate at half past three holds more of the city in one place than anywhere else all week. No one standing there is in a rush to move for the next ten minutes.

choices.label: Give the twins a job that is really theirs.
Ask everybody and sort it out when they arrive.
Split whoever comes into teams.

nodes.body: Anything said at the shop counter is all over town by supper. The story that spreads is the one Mira tells. So the words matter a lot more than the question.

choices.label: Show the new ones how a bracket holds.
Bring the Weaver in properly.
Give the twins a job that is really theirs.

nodes.body: The map and the ground disagree in nine spots. Only cycling the loop finds them. The full loop takes forty-one minutes at a work pace, longer with a tray. And a pencil beats a memory every single time.

choices.label: Respace the capsules for the real path.
Make the drop above the breach safe.
Mark the turns with something better than brass.

nodes.body: A marked route is not sixty-eight capsules. It is sixty-eight gaps. The gap that matters is the one where a messenger cannot see the next capsule from the last one. There are three of those on this wall, and none of them are marked.

choices.label: Find the sheltered hanging points.
Finish the survey properly before hanging anything.
Respace the capsules for the real path.

nodes.body: The clay above the Ropewalk turn is already greasy. The sky promises more rain after four. A capsule that shows a messenger the wrong side of that slope is worse than no capsule there at all.

choices.label: Make the drop above the breach safe.
Mark the turns with something better than brass.
Find the sheltered hanging points.

nodes.body: The school kitchen door stands open until four. The caretaker knows exactly where the festival hangings went and what came back with them. The walk home with a full box is uphill and takes both hands.

choices.label: Run a sealing line with the twins.
Fit the storm guards to the sealed ones.
Get the sealed trays to the top first.

nodes.body: Five sticks will seal about forty capsules properly, or sixty-eight badly. A badly sealed capsule does not fail at seven in the evening. It fails at ten past five, with the whole city watching the wall.

choices.label: Hold a reserve back at the loft.
Run a sealing line with the twins.
Fit the storm guards to the sealed ones.

nodes.body: One sealed capsule on the loft step with a watch beside it answers the only question that matters. Will the seal hold from now until the messengers are in? It costs twenty minutes to find out. It costs far more not to.

choices.label: Get the sealed trays to the top first.
Hold a reserve back at the loft.
Run a sealing line with the twins.

nodes.body: Between the inn, the guildhall and three kitchens, there are storm capsules, a signal lamp and a box of stubby candles in jars. None of them match the route, but all of them mark a spot.

choices.label: Fit the storm guards to the sealed ones.
Get the sealed trays to the top first.
Hold a reserve back at the loft.

nodes.body: Two on the stairs, two in the market, one on the turn and one running between them is a plan. Six people all starting at the loft and talking is not. The difference is whoever says the first sentence.

choices.label: Write the rota where people can see it.
Set up a runner between the two ends.
Get the kettle going at the loft.

nodes.body: Everybody who has never hung a capsule hangs the first one badly and the second one well. The ten minutes spent on that are the cheapest ten minutes of the whole afternoon.

choices.label: Put Master Fenn where he can see the wall.
Write the rota where people can see it.
Set up a runner between the two ends.

nodes.body: A handcart brings four trays up to the top of the wall. One person can only carry one. The cost of asking is a five-minute stop in a yard. You have to listen about gates with your hands behind your back.

choices.label: Get the kettle going at the loft.
Put Master Fenn where he can see the wall.
Write the rota where people can see it.

nodes.body: Kit and Ren will do a dull job well for an hour if it is truly theirs. They will do it badly for four minutes if it was made up to keep them busy. There is exactly one job on this circuit that fits them.

choices.label: Set up a runner between the two ends.
Get the kettle going at the loft.
Put Master Fenn where he can see the wall.

nodes.body: The ledger spaces them evenly, but the ground does not want them evenly. It wants them at the turns, at the drop, and at the two places where the walk looks like it goes somewhere it does not.

choices.label: Hang the top section to the new plan.
Cycle it in the half dark and look.
Keep four capsules for whatever is wrong.

nodes.body: Two capsules, a pole and a length of bright tape will say stop here in a way a tired person reads without thinking about it, and every one of those capsules comes out of the count the top of the route was relying on.

choices.label: Get a light onto the Ropewalk gate.
Hang the top section to the new plan.
Cycle it in the half dark and look.

nodes.body: Paint on a stone lasts longer than any capsule. The city has half a tin of white gate paint in the loft. The argument about painting stones on a wall has been going on since long before Master Fenn took the circuit.

choices.label: Keep four capsules for whatever is wrong.
Get a light onto the Ropewalk gate.
Hang the top section to the new plan.

nodes.body: The wind comes across the wall, not up it. This makes the leeward side of every parapet, post, and thorn on the circuit worth a capsule. That capsule will still be swinging at seven.

choices.label: Cycle it in the half dark and look.
Keep four capsules for whatever is wrong.
Get a light onto the Ropewalk gate.

nodes.body: A wax stick snaps on the loft step. It takes the afternoon with it: the grit is everywhere. The sand goes down. The tray has to be wiped out twice. By the time the yard is safe the light is going. The wall gets walked with hand lamps, and the capsules go up on Saturday.

Eleven people turn up at ten past four. They stand in the loft asking what to do while the light goes. By the time there is a list of who is doing what, the wall has gone grey. The capsules go up by lamplight, put up all crooked. Everybody agrees it was lovely to see everyone out.

The survey is done at ten past five. It is honest, complete, and truly useful. The wall is not yet marked. That evening the plan is rewritten at the kitchen table into something true. The capsules go up on Saturday in the light, with all knowing where they belong.

ending.title: A Very Good Map of a Dark Wall

nodes.body: One person seals. One wipes. One carries. The queue moves at the speed of the slowest job. That is always the wiping. Kit and Ren will hold that line for exactly as long as somebody keeps counting out loud.

choices.label: Plan for the ones that crack.
Get the wax sticks and matches sorted.
Count what is actually sealed.

nodes.body: The storm guards fit forty of the sixty-eight. They go on easily before a capsule is hung. They go on awfully afterwards in the wind. The ones without guards will have to hang where the wall shelters them. This means a different plan for the whole top half.

choices.label: Get a message to Aisling about the timing.
Seal fifty properly and leave the rest empty.
Plan for the ones that crack.

nodes.body: The top of the route is the furthest from the loft. It is the last place anybody wants to be cycling at five o'clock. The argument for doing it first gets harder to make with every ten minutes that passes.

choices.label: Get the wax sticks and matches sorted.
Count what is actually sealed.
Get a message to Aisling about the timing.

nodes.body: Six sealed capsules and a box are kept at the loft. They are either the most sensible thing anybody does today or six capsules of wall left dark. Which one it turns out to be depends entirely on what goes wrong later.

choices.label: Seal fifty properly and leave the rest empty.
Plan for the ones that crack.
Get the wax sticks and matches sorted.

nodes.body: A rota on a page in somebody's pocket is a rumour. A rota chalked on the loft door is a fact. The loft door carries a faint chalk mark from every spring back to when the capsules were tin.

choices.label: Have somebody check the top pair.
Keep the top half with the team that knows it.
Send two people up for the signal.

nodes.body: The top of the stairs cannot see the market. Neither end can hear the other. So a runner who knows both is worth more than a phone with no signal. It is also the coldest job on the wall and the one nobody volunteers for.

choices.label: Get everyone off the wall by six.
Let the city finish it however it likes.
Have somebody check the top pair.

nodes.body: A kettle at the loft at half past four is not a luxury. It is the thing that stops six people going home at five. Master Fenn can manage it one-handed if somebody else carries the water.

choices.label: Keep the top half with the team that knows it.
Send two people up for the signal.
Get everyone off the wall by six.

nodes.body: He cannot ride a bike or climb. But he can look at the wall from the loft steps and tell you which capsule is wrong from very far away. That is the one skill no one else on the wall has.

choices.label: Let the city finish it however it likes.
Have somebody check the top pair.
Keep the top half with the team that knows it.

nodes.body: The top part takes nineteen capsules with the new space. The tray that got to the top holds only sixteen. So one person must go back down the stairs. Or the last three spots stay empty.

choices.label: Close the last gap on the wall.
Go back for the two that blew out.
Go up and meet the party at the top.

nodes.body: By half past four, the wall is dark enough to test. Riding it in that light is the only way to see it as the messengers will. Two things that looked fine at three are now hard to see from above.

choices.label: Hold the bottom and let them come in.
Leave the shoulder and mark everything else.
Close the last gap on the wall.

nodes.body: Each spring, something goes wrong at the last minute that no one saw coming. Four capsules in a bag at the top of the stairs is the cheapest plan this city ever made.

choices.label: Go back for the two that blew out.
Go up and meet the party at the top.
Hold the bottom and let them come in.

nodes.body: The new gate is the one spot on the path where a rider must do more than just keep cycling. Doing something in the dark without a mark is where every fight about this walk has started.

choices.label: Leave the shoulder and mark everything else.
Close the last gap on the wall.
Go back for the two that blew out.

nodes.body: Some of the seals will crack, which is what the circuit means by the word ROUND written three times in the margin, and somebody has to be the person who cycles the whole route again at seven with a wax stick in a pouch.

choices.label: Wait at the top of the stairs.
Get the phone up to the signal.
Cycle the route counting what is sealed.

nodes.body: There are two boxes of matches. One is damp. There is also a bundle of wax sticks Master Fenn cut years ago. Sealing capsules in the wind is not a match job. It is a wax stick job. The time you save is about forty minutes.

choices.label: Fetch the hand lamps from the loft.
Go up the wall to meet them.
Get the loft ready for sixteen cold people.

nodes.body: The only true count is one someone has ridden out and made. The path has a tally box at the bottom. It has been marked in pencil every spring, since long before anyone here was born.

choices.label: Ask the Weaver for the handcart.
Take a wax stick to the shoulder.
Hold the plan and trust the route.

nodes.body: The party is coming in even if the wall is not marked. The useful message is a number and a time. It is not a promise. The signal at the top of the stairs lasts for about a minute. Then it stops and thinks.

choices.label: Wait at the top of the stairs.
Get the phone up to the signal.
Cycle the route counting what is sealed.

nodes.body: The two top capsules are the first ones the messengers see from the north road. They are also the ones no one bikes back to check. They hang in the worst wind with the least cover on the route.

choices.label: Fetch the hand lamps from the loft.
Go up the wall to meet them.
Get the loft ready for sixteen cold people.

nodes.body: The stair team learned the stairs in one day. They know just which parts turn in their holes. Passing that job to a new person at five costs more than the fresh legs are worth.

choices.label: Ask the Weaver for the handcart.
Take a wax stick to the shoulder.
Hold the plan and trust the route.

nodes.body: The phone signal at the top of the stairs is one bar and one person alone up there at dusk is how the rota rule about pairs came to be written in the first place, in capital letters, twice.

choices.label: Wait at the top of the stairs.
Get the phone up to the signal.
Cycle the route counting what is sealed.

nodes.body: The most important rule is not about capsules. Everyone who goes up must come down and be counted. This must happen before the messengers arrive. The counting is the part people often forget on a fun afternoon.

choices.label: Fetch the hand lamps from the loft.
Go up the wall to meet them.
Get the loft ready for sixteen cold people.

nodes.body: The gap from the top of the stairs to the first wall capsule is ninety empty paces. It is the part of the route a messenger meets first. They meet it tired.

choices.label: Ask the Weaver for the handcart.
Take a wax stick to the shoulder.
Hold the plan and trust the route.

nodes.body: Two capsules on the bare shoulder have blown off their hooks once already. They will do it again. The real question is if someone stands there with them. Or should they move them somewhere out of the wind?

choices.label: Wait at the top of the stairs.
Get the phone up to the signal.
Cycle the route counting what is sealed.

nodes.body: Cycling up to meet sixteen people from the north road turns a marked route into a welcome. It means being out on the wall in the dark on purpose. That is different from being out by accident. It is harder to explain later on.

choices.label: Fetch the hand lamps from the loft.
Go up the wall to meet them.
Get the loft ready for sixteen cold people.

nodes.body: Standing at the market stile with a lamp and just watching the wall do its job is harder. That is the choice the rota was built around. Either the route is good enough now, or it is not.

choices.label: Ask the Weaver for the handcart.
Take a wax stick to the shoulder.
Hold the plan and trust the route.

nodes.body: Fifty go up sealed properly. Eighteen stay in the tray. The dusk does more of the work than anyone expected. The messengers come in easily. They never know there was a plan at all. The tally box gets a fifty in it. There is a note beside it about the missing box.

ending.title: Fifty Capsules and a Clear Dusk

nodes.body: The wall gets marked by sixteen people. They mostly did not know each other at three o clock. Half the capsules hang at slightly wrong heights because of it. The circuit goes back in the wrap. Thirteen new names are written into the column. One of them is underlined.

The route is marked from end to end, except for one part on the shoulder. That part swallows two capsules twice. The messengers come in chatting. They never notice the gap they crossed. The tally box says sixty-six. The note beside it says shoulder, again.

Sunset goes by. The wall is marked and nobody is on it. The north road above is a flat grey where sixteen people ought to be. Ten minutes late off a road means nothing at all. Forty minutes means something.

choices.label: Move the six to the leeward side.
Send a pair up with the spare bag.
Put a capsule at the market corner.

nodes.body: One bar at the top stair. A message Aisling sent twenty minutes ago arrives all at once. They are down off the high road. One of them has turned an ankle. They are moving slower than the light is going.

choices.label: Set a relay along the marked stretch.
Keep the signal watch at the top stair.
Get help to the messenger with the ankle.

nodes.body: Sixty marked, six off their hooks and two never hung, and the six that are off sit inside the same two hundred paces on the exposed shoulder where the wind comes across the wall.

choices.label: Wait at the Ropewalk gate with a light.
Finish the tally and write it down.
Go round once more with the wax stick.

nodes.body: The loft cupboard holds four hand lamps. Two of them have oil in them. That is exactly the sort of fact the circuit exists to record. It does not record it anywhere.

choices.label: Stand where you are and let the wall do its work.
Get them in before the weather closes in.
Count them in and check the tally.

nodes.body: Going up means riding away from every mark on the route. It means going onto the part of the wall that has never had a capsule on it. It also means that someone at the bottom knows exactly where you have gone and when.

choices.label: Rewrite the circuit while it is all still fresh.
Stay on the shoulder and watch what the wind does.
Give the turn the last two capsules.

nodes.body: The loft has a kettle and a brazier that works. It also has the wrong number of stools. Sixteen people are off a north road at six on an autumn evening. They want all three of those more than they want a lovely wall.

choices.label: Move the six to the leeward side.
Send a pair up with the spare bag.
Put a capsule at the market corner.

nodes.body: The handcart will get up the walk to the Ropewalk turn in four minutes. It can do it with a person and a bag on the back. Asking for it a second time in one afternoon is a different sort of asking.

choices.label: Set a relay along the marked stretch.
Keep the signal watch at the top stair.
Get help to the messenger with the ankle.

nodes.body: Six capsules off in one stretch is not bad luck. It is the wind finding the one place nobody thought enough about. Re-hanging them where they swung means doing it all again in twenty minutes.

choices.label: Wait at the Ropewalk gate with a light.
Finish the tally and write it down.
Go round once more with the wax stick.

nodes.body: The route is marked. The rota is written. The tally is counted. The urge now is to keep changing things. There is a version of this evening where the best thing anyone does is nothing at all.

choices.label: Stand where you are and let the wall do its work.
Get them in before the weather closes in.
Count them in and check the tally.

nodes.body: Moving a capsule in the dark means unhooking, carrying, and rehanging with cold hands. The leeward line is nine paces off the walk. That is nine paces of mark the messengers will not get.

choices.label: Cycle them in and get the door open.
See them safely round the turn.
Get the top pair hung before they clear the high road.

nodes.body: Four spare capsules, a wax stick, a pouch, and two people who know the shoulder can close the dark stretch in twelve minutes. The pair must be back down before the party reaches the turn.

choices.label: Send the cart up with the last tray.
Fill in the tally box and hang the circuit back up.
Hand the circuit back to Master Fenn.

nodes.body: The market corner is where the lime trees hide the turn. A tired party with a hurt ankle will make its one mistake of the evening there. A storm capsule on the gatepost fixes it outright.

choices.label: Write down what the circuit should have said.
Mark what is left after they are in.
Leave the shoulder to the wind and go down.

nodes.body: Three people spaced along the marked stretch can pass a message from the north road to the loft in under two minutes. They do not need any signal at all. This uses the three people who were going to cycle up anyway.

choices.label: Cycle them in and get the door open.
See them safely round the turn.
Get the top pair hung before they clear the high road.

nodes.body: One pair on the top stair hold the phone at the exact angle that works. This is how the city hears what is happening on the north road. It is twenty minutes of standing still in the wind, doing what looks like nothing.

choices.label: Send the cart up with the last tray.
Fill in the tally box and hang the circuit back up.
Hand the circuit back to Master Fenn.

nodes.body: A turned ankle three hundred paces above the Ropewalk gate needs a shoulder. It needs a light. It needs someone who does not fuss. The cart can meet them at the turn, if the gate is open and a person stands at it.

choices.label: Write down what the circuit should have said.
Mark what is left after they are in.
Leave the shoulder to the wind and go down.

nodes.body: The gate is the pinch point of the whole evening. There are sixteen people, one hurt one, a chained hinge, and a yard of dye vats. Whoever stands there with a lamp decides how the next ten minutes go.

choices.label: Cycle them in and get the door open.
See them safely round the turn.
Get the top pair hung before they clear the high road.

nodes.body: The tally box wants a number. The margin wants the truth. This year the truth has a missing box, a gate, a hole, and six capsules that will not stay hung on the shoulder.

choices.label: Send the cart up with the last tray.
Fill in the tally box and hang the circuit back up.
Hand the circuit back to Master Fenn.

nodes.body: One more round of the whole route at ten to six. Fix whatever has cracked. That is the oldest rule on the circuit, and it is written in the steadiest hand.

choices.label: Write down what the circuit should have said.
Mark what is left after they are in.
Leave the shoulder to the wind and go down.

nodes.body: The party comes off the north road into a line of capsules. It runs without a break from the top of the stairs to the market stile. Sixteen people cycle down talking about the view. Nothing big happens anywhere on the wall. That has been the aim of the circuit since 1927.

The last person reaches the market stile at twenty-five past six. That's ten minutes before the rain. The capsules are still swinging behind them all the way up the wall. Aisling counts sixteen twice and then stops counting.

Sixty-six up. Sixteen messengers in. Six people off the wall. All of it is written in the tally box in pencil before anyone sits down. This is the first year in three that the numbers on the page and the numbers on the wall are the same numbers.

The circuit gets rewritten on the loft table. The dust is still on everybody. The new one has the breach in it, the gate in it, the shoulder in it. It also has thirteen true names. Master Fenn signs the bottom with his left hand. It is barely readable.

Twenty minutes on the shoulder with a wax stick teaches more about that stretch than nine springs of hanging capsules on it. The gusts come in threes across the wall. Nothing hung on the walk side lives past the second gust. The party cycles in without you. The notebook fills up.

ending.title: What the Wind Does on the Shoulder

nodes.body: The turn is marked. The top of the stairs is not. The party comes down the stairs in the dark with one hand lamp shared by sixteen. Nobody falls. Everybody notices. The stairs get talked about at the loft. They use the voice the city keeps for near misses.

ending.title: Two Capsules Short at the Stairs

nodes.body: Sixteen people, one strapped ankle, and six capsule keepers come through the loft door. It is twenty to seven. The room has a working brazier and the wrong number of stools. The wall behind them is still swinging end to end in the rain.

The new line above the Ropewalk does just what it was rehung to do. Sixteen people cycle the turn. Not one of them drifts onto the old edge above the breach. And not one of them sees there was ever a choice to make there.

From the north road the wall shows as a line of small brass glints a mile off. Aisling says later that the party stopped pedaling for a moment when they came over the last rise and saw it. That is the whole point of the capsules. It is not written down anywhere on the circuit.

ending.title: A Wall You Could See From the North Road

nodes.body: The cart takes the last tray and two people to the Ropewalk turn in four minutes. The gate stands open with a lamp on the post. The Weaver stands beside it in the rain. He tells every person who passes that this is his yard.

The tally box gets its number. The margin gets four true lines about the shoulder. The clipboard goes back on its nail in the loft with the pencil on the string. Next spring starts from a page that is not lying.

The circuit comes back with a fixed part, a rewritten part, a new name, and wax on the corner of page two. Master Fenn reads it with his hand on the table. He says only that it will do. From him, that is a great deal.

ending.title: Handed Back Better Than It Came

nodes.body: The evening ends with the wall half marked. There is a page of notes that nobody asked for. The notes tell where the walk really goes, what the wind does, which brackets turn, and how long the stairs take with a tray. It is the most useful thing written about this walk in years. It marked nothing at all tonight.

ending.title: The Page That Should Have Been There

nodes.body: The party is home before the wall is finished. The last fourteen capsules go up at seven in the rain for nobody. They swing over an empty walk. It is pretty. The wind takes four of them at nine.

The shoulder goes dark for the third time and stays dark. Sixteen people cross two hundred paces of it on one hand lamp. The rain comes in sideways. Everybody gets down and nobody is hurt. Nobody says the wall was marked this year.
